newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends strong, July hits one-week high.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends strong, July hits one-week high.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed stronger across the board on Wednesday, but traders still saw prices trapped in a wide range.

July closed up 15 stg at 1,004 stg per tonne while September rose 13 to 1,018. Total volume stood at 6,845 lots, with December tallying 1,702 and March notching 1,530. July came in third with 1,515 contracts. All other months traded fewer than 900 lots.
Despite July's move up to the highest level since April 29 by one stg, traders said cocoa still looked rangebound between the April 2 high of 1,065 and the April 9 low of 980.
Before 1,065, traders pegged intial July resistance at 1,015.
Traders said light industry and speculative buying coupled with light short-covering in the morning boosted prices up to session highs but eased off by the afternooon.
Switches were most active with December 1997/March 1998 trading 1,000 contracts at 12 stg, traders said. The December/March spread closed up one stg at 13.
A large trade house was also seen crossing September 700 times at 19 stg.
Arbitrage was also noted against New York in the afternoon, but the activity was light.
Traders in Hamburg said on Wednesday cash cocoa buyers have disappeared after taking advantage of a post-election slide in sterling last week.
They said the industry had signalled buying interest at favourable sterling levels and below 1,000 stg in the July future here.
Cocoa butter demand was flat though the butter ratio over futures had fallen by about 15 points over the past six weeks.
Traders here said the market was waiting for some fundamental news about supply or demand to prod prices out of their recent range.
News Cadbury workers voted overwhelmingly in favour of a strike at the Bournville plant in England had little impact on prices.
No cocoa options traded at LIFFE.
